correctness.rationale: For a rooted passive zero-input system with known positive k_v,b_v and root measurement c x_r, the v-th transfer numerator is c g_v times the product over vertices outside the root-to-v path of (s+k_u). The monic characteristic denominator gives a unit-lower-triangular change from the first n outlet derivative coefficients to these polynomials. Leaf deletion and monic synthetic division give the exact determinant recursion with factor c g_leaf times the product of rate differences against incomparable earlier vertices. Induction covers all n and all positive rates including repeated ones; the n=1 base is c. The rank criterion follows directly; Cayley-Hamilton extends a zero initial jet to an identical entire curve, and perturbations of a strictly positive initial vector yield positive indistinguishable states. A standalone SymPy checker independently confirms the determinant on 34 symbolically parameterized rooted trees and 665 seeded exact-rational networks, including 105 singular cases. Those finite tests are not substitutes for the general induction.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality is confined to the exact all-parameter, all-rooted-tree observability determinant with edge-path weights and differences indexed precisely by incomparable vertex pairs. This is stronger than asserting generic observability or that identical sibling rates can hide states. The full 1986 study of hidden generalized-tree modes was unavailable and may imply the qualitative obstruction; its abstract does not establish the explicit determinant identity. Historical priority remains provisional and is not independently certified.

value.rationale: An outlet hydrograph is a natural physically meaningful single-sensor bottleneck in branched drainage. The exact determinant identifies all algebraic losses of recoverable stored-volume information and explains why equal recession times on branches—but not in series—create indistinguishable initial states. Its explicit path-transfer product also flags weak sensitivity as branch rates approach collision. This is a structural all-network-size theorem, not a routine application of numerical rank to one chosen catchment. Its scope excludes unknown inputs, nonlinear flow and noisy inversion.
